commit 1c7b62c73ce8cd6bf408c0abeb5644040f94639c
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 9 19:47:07 2026 +0800

    behavioral: andes-sim `run --model accurate` (F8)
    
    Add the second standalone model: one cycle-accurate engine alone, from reset
    (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough -- the ELF plus the
    post-`--` args become the engine's own command line, run with inherited stdio,
    no timeout, exit code propagated. Cycles surface in the engine's native output.
    
    Engine selection is registry-driven (F2): resolve_accurate_engine() picks the
    cycle-accurate engine from the discovered set -- an explicit --engine, else the
    sole one. It errors clearly on none ("build one with: andes-sim build --what
    vsim"), more than one (ambiguous; names the candidates), an --engine that
    matches nothing, or one that is functional rather than cycle-accurate. The
    predicate is kind=="cycle-accurate", so a future alioth/sid is eligible with no
    code change. run_accurate then reuses the F8 structural run_standalone() spine,
    so fast and accurate share the lone-ELF-plus-passthrough exec path verbatim.
    
    TDD: resolve_accurate_engine's six selection branches are unit-tested in
    run_test.cpp (RED via a returns-null stub, then GREEN). The new acceptance
    tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f8.sh drives the full discover -> resolve ->
    run_standalone -> exec path with throwaway "engine" scripts that ship the same
    standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}); it proves the done-when
    "selecting a different built <cfg> runs the other binary" deterministically,
    plus every error path. A guarded best-effort layer attempts a real vsim run
    (skips when the hybrid-oriented fixture does not terminate standalone).

# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F8 contract: `run --model accurate` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
#
#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
#      this exercises the exact argv path.
#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
#      the deterministic proof.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andes-sim-run-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"

# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"
  cat >"$f" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"verilator","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
else
  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
fi
EOF
  chmod +x "$f"
}

D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
mkengine "$D1" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v1 "verilator:v1" cycle-accurate m1
mkengine "$D2" v2 "verilator:v2" cycle-accurate m2
mkengine "$DF" f0 "verilator:f0" functional    fm

# expect WANT_RC REGEX -- cmd...: run cmd, assert exit code + combined-output match
expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*verilator:v1.*verilator:v2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v1 dummy.elf
expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:v2 dummy.elf
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --model accurate dummy.elf
# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for accurate
expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:f0 dummy.elf
# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
expect 2 "no engine 'verilator:nope'" \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate --engine verilator:nope dummy.elf
# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate
expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
  env ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --model accurate a.elf b.elf
echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"

# 3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort)
SIM=$(ls "$ROOT"/verilator/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"
if [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
  # The current fixtures are hybrid-oriented and loop forever standalone (no
  # exit path without QEMU's semihosting), so this caps the attempt: a cycle
  # line confirms the done-when; a timeout (rc 124) only confirms vsim launched
  # and is running, which is still useful. Either way -> not a failure.
  out=$(timeout 45 "$BIN" run --model accurate ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "[0-9]+ cycles simulated"; then

# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 is launched with
